question.text: Two trains <math> <mtext>A</mtext> </math> and <math> <mtext>B</mtext> </math> of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mtext>400 m</mtext></math> each are moving on two parallel tracks with a uniform speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>72</mn><mo> </mo><mfrac><mi>km</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">h</mi></mfrac></math> in the same direction, with <math> <mtext>A</mtext> </math> ahead of <math> <mtext>B</mtext></math>. The driver of <math> <mtext>B</mtext> </math> decides to overtake <math> <mtext>A</mtext> </math> and accelerates by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1 </mn><mfrac><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac></math>. If after <math> <mrow> <mtext>50 s</mtext></mrow></math>, the guard of <math> <mtext>B</mtext> </math> just brushes past the driver of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mtext>A</mtext></math> and the original distance between them is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>, then calculate value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>10</mn></mfrac></math> ?

solution.text:
Length of each train,

l⁡ A = l⁡ B = 4 0 0  m

u⁡A⁡=72×518m/s

= 20 m/s

Distance travelled by train A in 50 s

s A = u A × t

(As for unaccelerated motion, distance = Speed x Time)

s A = 2 0 × 5 0

= 1000 m

Distance travelled by train B in 50 s,

s B = u B t + 1 2 a B t 2

(As motion of train B is an accelerated motion)

s B = 2 0 × 5 0 + 1 2 × 1 × 5 0 2

= 1000 + 1250

= 2250 m

relative distance between the two trains =S B − S A

= 2250 - 1000

= 1250 m
we should subtract 2l from it where l is length of train so final answer will be 450 m

Alternate Method

Initially, both the trains are moving with same speed, the train B first comes that of the train A in 50 s with an acceleration of 50 s .

∴   Original distance between the trains

= Distance covered by train B with an acceleration a

= ut + 1 2 at 2

= 0 × 5 0 + 1 2 × 1 × 5 0 2

(As both train starts with same velocity, so velocity, so velocity of train when it starts accelerating can be taken as zero).

= 1250 m .

we should subtract 2l from it where l is length of train so final answer will be 450 m
